title: What Was Royal Patronage?
imageAlt: A teaching guide for What Was Royal Patronage?. It separates institutional relationships, recorded actions and limits without prescribing religious practice.
content:
Patronato Real means royal patronage. In this colonial setting it refers to arrangements linking the Spanish Crown with Catholic institutions and missionary work, involving support, responsibilities and royal influence over church affairs. It is an institutional relationship, not a name for every person's religious belief.

The monarchy and religious institutions were distinct even when their work overlapped. Do not imagine that every official was a priest, that every missionary was a governor, or that political support proves universal conversion. This history also differs from present-day arrangements.

Try a fictional museum-label task. A caption says royal support for a mission meant that all residents accepted its teachings. Separate the relationship between institutions from the evidence of local responses. One claim does not establish the other.

The diagram is an introductory model, not a complete legal chart for every year. Studying it does not require a prayer, a profession of faith or disclosure of your own beliefs.
clues: The term
Patronato Real refers here to royal patronage connecting Crown and Catholic institutions.
Different participants
Connected institutions did not make every official and religious worker the same person or role.
A limit
Institutional support does not establish everyone's belief or local consent.
task: Which description fits Patronato Real in this mission?
A royal-patronage relationship involving Crown and Catholic institutions
Proof every resident adopted one religion
A title making every priest a governor
A rule requiring students to profess a faith
reason: Royal patronage linked institutions through support and authority. It is not evidence of universal belief or identical roles.
definition: An arrangement through which a monarchy supports and exercises recognized influence in particular institutions.

title: Support Had to Become an Action
imageAlt: A teaching guide for Support Had to Become an Action. It separates institutional relationships, recorded actions and limits without prescribing religious practice.
content:
Missionary work required journeys, resources and people. Royal patronage involved material support for religious activity. A promise of support, a recorded allocation and evidence of actual use are different stages.

Historical discussions describe the Crown's support for missions, but that does not mean every promised resource arrived or every community experienced the same effect. To investigate a named case, ask what was promised, what was provided, who used it and what happened afterward.

Work through a fictional comparison. A document authorizes supplies for a mission; a second record shows only part of the supplies delivered. The authorization supports an intended allocation. It does not justify reporting that every planned item was received and used. These are classroom records, not original archive documents.

Keep local participants visible alongside officials and religious workers. Resources used for an institution cannot by themselves establish that all residents welcomed it, benefited equally or shared its teachings.
clues: Material support
Patronage could provide resources for missionary activity. An allocation is different from its actual use.
Trace the stages
Check the promise, delivery and use separately rather than assume all three occurred identically.
Check the effect
Funding alone does not reveal every community's benefits, burdens or beliefs.
task: A record authorizes mission supplies but gives no delivery evidence. What is careful?
Report the authorization and seek evidence of delivery and use
Declare every supply arrived and benefited everyone
Assume the allocation proves universal religious acceptance
Invent a receipt to complete the story
reason: Separate intended support from delivery, use and effects. Material provision does not establish universal acceptance.
definition: Resources assigned for a particular purpose.

title: Influence Did Not Erase Every Other Role
imageAlt: A teaching guide for Influence Did Not Erase Every Other Role. It separates institutional relationships, recorded actions and limits without prescribing religious practice.
content:
Royal patronage included influence in church administration, including presentation of candidates for certain church offices. Presentation means formally putting forward a candidate in an institutional process. It should not be turned into a claim that the monarch personally performed every religious duty or that one step completed every appointment.

Church authorities and royal representatives had distinct responsibilities. Which office acted and which procedure applied must be checked for the place, period and position. This introduction does not give one unchanging appointment sequence for all colonial offices.

Try a fictional process check. A record says a candidate was proposed for a position. It establishes a proposal, not every later approval or the person's conduct after taking office. More evidence is needed for those questions.

Use the model to separate connected roles. An institutional claim of authority is not the private belief of everyone affected, and a formal responsibility does not prove it was always carried out fairly.
clues: A formal role
The Crown had recognized influence in presenting candidates for certain church offices.
Separate procedure from outcome
A proposed candidate is not proof of every later approval or performance.
Keep historical context
Responsibilities and procedures need their own period and office, not one universal modern chart.
task: A record says a candidate was presented for a church office. Which conclusion stays within it?
A formal proposal occurred; later steps and performance need evidence
Every appointment step was completed automatically
The monarch personally performed every religious duty
All residents approved of the candidate
reason: Distinguish royal influence, church responsibilities and separate procedural steps. A proposal is not every later outcome.
definition: Formally putting forward a candidate for consideration in an institutional process.

title: Connected Institutions Could Disagree
imageAlt: A teaching guide for Connected Institutions Could Disagree. It separates institutional relationships, recorded actions and limits without prescribing religious practice.
content:
Institutions can cooperate and disagree. The history of royal patronage includes disputes over responsibilities and jurisdiction. Jurisdiction means the matters or area over which an authority claims responsibility. A disagreement between officials does not prove that all cooperation ended or that one participant represented every local voice.

Historical research on Manila's religious institutions examines disputes among governors, bishops and other church officials in particular periods. Keep those cases attached to their settings rather than treating every year as the same conflict. The lesson does not ask you to choose which present-day religion is correct.

For a fictional source exercise, one letter claims a decision belongs to a royal representative, while another claims a church authority should decide. First identify the disagreement. Then ask which procedures and later actions help establish its outcome. Do not invent a final ruling if it is missing.

A record of conflict helps test the claim that linked institutions always acted as one. It still needs evidence to explain what happened to communities.
clues: Overlap
Connected responsibilities could produce cooperation as well as disagreements over authority.
A claim in context
A letter stating a jurisdictional claim is not automatically a final accepted decision.
Outcome remains a question
Compare procedures and later evidence; a dispute alone does not show who prevailed or every local effect.
task: Two fictional letters claim different authorities should decide. What does this establish most directly?
A disagreement that needs procedural and later evidence to assess the outcome
Proof that linked institutions never cooperated
Proof that the first writer always won
Everyone's private belief about the issue
reason: Institutional connection did not mean constant agreement. Claims, decisions and local effects must be investigated separately.
definition: The matters or area over which an authority has responsibilities or claims authority.

title: Institutional Records Are Not All Voices
imageAlt: A teaching guide for Institutional Records Are Not All Voices. It separates institutional relationships, recorded actions and limits without prescribing religious practice.
content:
An official instruction, a religious report and a local request can emphasize different parts of a relationship. None automatically contains every person's experience. Studying royal patronage should not leave affected communities out of the story.

A record that resources supported a mission may answer a question about provision. It does not by itself reveal whether particular people accepted teachings, disputed demands or experienced benefits and burdens. Claims about those responses need appropriate evidence, just as in Mission 1.

Try a fictional report check. An official describes a supported institution as successful, but the supplied evidence only records a payment. Keep the documented action and identify the unsupported claim about universal success. Compare other sources where possible instead of filling missing voices with invented speech.

Respect the difference between historical analysis and religious judgment. A student can examine power, duties and effects without practising a religion or treating one institutional account as the measure of all people's worth.
clues: Identify the action
An instruction, allocation and account of effects are different kinds of evidence.
Include affected people
An institutional writer's purpose does not establish every resident's response or belief.
State the missing evidence
A recorded payment alone cannot prove universal success, consent or benefit.
task: A report records support but claims universal success. What is missing?
Evidence of actual outcomes and affected people's responses
Only a larger name for the institution
A statement that payments always prove acceptance
An invented speech of everyone's approval
reason: Institutional support and claimed success are different. Include local evidence and identify what remains uncertain.
definition: A record written from the position or purposes of an organized body.

title: Your Royal Patronage Evidence Report
imageAlt: A report guide separates institutional support, formal roles, procedural steps and evidence of local effects. It does not complete the chapter or assess religious belief.
content: Explain royal patronage as a relationship rather than a claim that all roles and beliefs became identical. Identify support for religious work, recognized influence in institutional matters and the distinct responsibilities of participants. Trace the action before judging the outcome. An allocation is not actual delivery; a proposed candidate is not every later approval; a disputed claim is not a final accepted decision. Look for evidence of later actions and effects on people. Use this fictional report frame in your own words: The record shows [support, role or claim]. It concerns [institution, place and period]. To establish [later outcome or local response], we need [further evidence]. This is a classroom guide, not an original quotation or religious instruction. The quiz checks historical reasoning, not your faith. Revisit difficult topics and use targeted practice before retrying. Passing earns the mission reward once. Complete all missions, then pass the chapter challenge to earn the chapter badge.
clues: Explain the relationship
Keep Crown, church institutions and local participants distinct even when their activities overlap.
Separate stages
Distinguish support, proposals, claims and actual outcomes.
Include source limits
Assess records without inventing universal belief or missing local voices.
task: Which explanation best connects the mission ideas?
Royal patronage linked support and authority, while procedures, disagreements and local effects need their own evidence
A payment proves everyone shared one belief
A proposed candidate proves every later step and fair outcome
Linked institutions never had distinct responsibilities
reason: Explain royal patronage through institutional relationships and documented actions while keeping later outcomes and local responses open to evidence.
definition: An explanation of the past built by comparing evidence and its limits.
